sections.text: This procedure details the outlines steps required for dismantling and overhauling station equipment for the major maintenance activities P2 which are performed every 10 years as indicated by Y10 in the above title block.

items: Work permit must be issued.
Circuit breaker must be isolated and properly earthed.
Isolate the DC control voltage.
Wear safety, Helmet shoes --------- etc.
Caution marks must be hanged on a work place.
Safety robe around a work place.
Before using a blower to clean all compartment of the circuit breaker from dust, wear your breathing mask to protect your lung tissues from the dust particulate.
Dont burn the cloth used in cleaning, collect it and send it to the dumb.
The fans must be operated & the doors must be open.
SF6 leaks also have bad impact on the environment.
Complete tool bag.
Grease gun, Lockotite
Crane.
Wool wires.
Portable gauge, Portable Gas leakage detector.

Wrench for coil, 
 all special tools,

Make sure that the CB is isolated from all the AC & DC
 sources.

Remove the relays which cause a suddenly trip due to under
 pressure of the gas in the other breakers.
Discharge the SF6 gas from the chamber.

Disconnect the contact of the pressure switch from the
 control cables.

Using spectral tool no. 32 to raise the moving contact and
 fix it by ruler so the arc chamber and hydraulic mechanism have separated
 and the moving at on position.

Disassemble the support shunt of current transformer Figure
 52.

Conductor bar of 3 phase must be fixed along current TR side
 in balanced position using special tool no 37 Figure 53, Figure 54.

Flanges to current transformer have to be disassembled
 Figure 55.

Through top flange the ARC chamber must be tied and all
 fixation bolts of arc chamber base disassemble Figure 56.
All CT's flange bolts have to be dismantled.

Using the crane shaft the arc chamber to up about 2-mm
 Figure 57.

Using the crane take the arc chamber out of its location
 about 2.5 cm Figure 58.

To fix the conductor bar you have to be used special tool No
 40 to circuit breaker side Figure 60, 61.

Using plastic sheet you have to be covered all opining parts
 to avoid the dust.

Using the crane take the arc chamber out its location to
 maintenance location putting it an wood support Figure 62, 63.
Dismantle the top flange of arc chamber.

Tie the fixed contact and take it out of the
 chamber (Figure 1a) and put it on the maintenance table Figure 1b, 1c.

Dismantle the lower flange to reach to moving
 contacts and disassemble it. Take moving contacts out of arc chamber, both
 arc chamber house and moving contact are separate. Good inspection for
 moving and fixed contacts. A good cleaning for all parts and the arc chamber
 cylinder. Using plastic sheet to cover all components of the arc chamber to
 a void dust accumulation.

The lower block nut no. 36 of circuit breaker
 must be dismantling at make you able to draw the insulator drive through the
 cone.

All gas sealing must be change according to
 its drawing position for the arc chamber fig 60, 62, and 63.

Using white alcohol all parts you have to
 ensure that the surface contacts for moving and fixed are good and there is
 ma deterioration.

Using smooth sandpaper, remove and smooth
 contact surface deterioration.

Inner diameter of arc chamber nozzle must be
 checked according to manual instruction values and change it is necessary
 you have to ensure that there is no evaporation in tungsten part.

All arc chamber cylinder gaskets must be
 changed.
Grease gas seal chamber using grease gun.

Put the chamber casing on the moving contact
 using the crane you have to.

All lower flange gaskets no. 112 B, no. 113 B
 must be changed.

Assemble the fixed contact and all tighter
 flange gaskets must be changed.

To facilitate the smelling used water balance
 to adjust the ARC chamber level after raising by the crane.

All circuit breaker and CT conductor must be
 cleaned by alcohol wet clothe to avoid dust and impurities accumulate.

Take care during transfer the arc chamber to
 its location. Using the crane to adjust the CT and circuit breaker together
 in vertical and horizontal position.

Arc chamber lower flange and circuit breaker
 base must le tied together in correct horizontal position with required
 momentum.

Assemble and fix the accumulator in its
 location-using crane and also connect the accumulator flange and hose.

Ram of arc chamber and motor shaft of
 hydraulic mechanism must be connected using special tool no. 22a, to remove
 the ruler and draw the arc chamber, ram all bolts and nuts must he well tied
 using key 19.

Fill the 3 oil tanks for circuit breaker to
 standard level of oil on each tank.

At first you have to start oil pump operation
 for short time

Anther once yew have to start oil pump
 operation and open the air output valve to release the air during oil pump
 operation to get a required pressure of the pump.

Oil bleeding have to be done through a
 concern valve for low pressure consequently through high-pressure valve for
 several times to remote air from oil during switches on & off.

Check the oil pressure during the previous
 procedures and also oil pressure settings for pressure switch according to
 manufacturer instructions as follow:
 - Normal pressure 330 bar
 - Pump start 320 bar
 - Pump stop 335 bar
 - Off automation 227 bar
 - Block on 270 bar Safety valve open on 390
 bar Safety valve close on 345 bar

items:
Start a vacuum procedure for circuit breaker until 0.5 m bar
 for 24 hours. Pressure gauge have to be checked periodically to ensure there
 is no leak and you can wait for half hour if there is leak you have to
 herised all bolt and flames righting it if it necessary.

Charge nitrogen gas to 2 bar for 12 hours. Reduce the
 nitrogen gas pressure until 1 bar and you have to unite for 12 hours after
 that discharge the nitrogen to reach zero bar.

Then respite the vacuum procedures until 0.5 for 12 hours.
 After that restart to charge the SF6 gas to normal operation pressure 6.55
 bar for circuit breaker.
Timing test
Contact resistance test
Dew point test
Gas percentage test
Acidity test

Introduction
